_: THIS REPO'S OWN context budget — BL-37 half (a), provisioned by S90 (2026-08-15) from starter-kit/context-budget.json and then CALIBRATED, per that seed's own instruction to replace every inherited number with one defensible from a measurement of this project. This repo AUTHORS and DISTRIBUTES the FM #28 gate (bin/_manifest.py:54 ships starter-kit/context_budget.py -> adopter context_budget.py, :60 ships the seed -> adopter .context-budget.json) and until now had never configured it for itself — the same blind-at-home shape as BL-29 and upstream issue #59, arriving through configuration rather than path resolution. Run: python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py (there is no root copy of the tool here; see _tool_location below).
_tool_location: The tool is NOT at this repo's root. bin/_manifest.py installs it at ADOPTER roots; canonically it lives only at starter-kit/context_budget.py. Two consequences, both measured not assumed: (1) invoke it as `python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py` — find_root() then walks up to this repo root via .git and reads this file, which is why a root-relative `path` below still resolves; (2) `install-hook` would write a hook that execs $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/context_budget.py, which does not exist here, AND this clone already sets core.hooksPath=.githooks whose pre-commit is the FM #27 ledger gate, so install-hook correctly declines with 'already exists and is not ours'. The budget gate is therefore MEASURING here, not BLOCKING. Wiring it into .githooks/pre-commit would edit a canonical file that ships upstream — deliberately not done here; raised as a follow-on instead.
_bytes_per_token: MEASURED ON THIS REPO, 2026-08-15 (S90). Regression of each session's opening context on the size of CLAUDE.md at that session's start, over n=75 transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/-Users-rmsharp-Development-methodology: opening_tokens ~= 42,033.2 + 0.356891 x bytes, R^2 = 0.8083 => 2.8020 B/tok, rounded here to 2.80. Corroborated by two independent local instruments: the same fit with only the lineage defect corrected gives 2.93 (R^2 = 0.6854), and the natural experiment across commit 7603f10 (CLAUDE.md 52,909 -> 8,519 B, -44,390 B) using the two sessions bracketing it within 20 minutes on each side gives 44,390 B / 17,616 tok = 2.52. Three local estimates spanning 2.52-2.93, and the seed's 2.93 from a different project, all agree within ~15%. THE TOOL NOW AGREES — BL-38 FIXED IT (S91, 2026-08-15). The warning that used to live in this key said `--calibrate` prints 14.45 B/tok at R^2 = 0.0513 and must not be adopted; that is no longer true and the key would otherwise have become a false claim about a tool that had been repaired. The two defects behind it (D1: `git log -- CLAUDE.md` walked ALL merged ancestry, so upstream's own CLAUDE.md lineage interleaved with this fork's by commit date and 'size at time T' stopped being a function; D2: ISO timestamps were sorted and compared AS STRINGS across mixed offsets) are fixed in starter-kit/context_budget.py. Re-run `python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py --calibrate` rather than trusting this sentence: at n=76 it prints 2.81 B/tok at R^2 = 0.8054, against the 2.80 recorded here from S90's n=75. The small drift is the extra transcript, not a disagreement. A fit below R^2 = 0.50 is now REFUSED by the tool rather than printed, so this key can no longer be 'corrected' to noise by a session that reads the number and not the statistic.
_fixed_harness_tokens: MEASURED — the intercept of the same n=75 fit above: the opening context that exists before any budgeted file is loaded (system prompt, tool schemas, skill listings, MCP server tools, agent-level memory). The seed carries 35,700 from a different project and a different harness configuration; this repo's floor is higher. Note what this makes CLAUDE.md worth: at 11,064 B and 2.80 B/tok it is 3,951 tok, 9.4% of this floor.
_growth_run: INHERITED FROM THE SEED, NOT DERIVED — and labelled so rather than presented as measured. It cannot be calibrated on day one: this repo has no .context-budget-history.jsonl until this config's first run, so the series the trigger reads is empty. Revisit once ~15 measurements exist; the honest input is how many consecutive non-shrinking readings this repo actually produces between deliberate reductions (S23, S24, S25, S87 and S89 were all reductions, so the true run length here is probably short).

resident._: Resident is a ONE-FILE class in this repo — CLAUDE.md is the only artifact the harness injects in full before the session starts; this repo has no root SESSION_RUNNER.md (its runner is the distributed starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md) and no root SESSION_NOTES.md (its continuity record is HANDOFFS.md). So this total equals CLAUDE.md's own ceiling by construction. That is deliberate and it is NOT a check that cannot fail: the per-file ceiling cannot see a SECOND resident file being added, and this one can. Agent-level memory (~/.claude/projects/.../MEMORY.md) is genuinely resident too but is per-operator and per-machine, outside this repo, and not a reviewable diff — deliberately excluded, and worth remembering when reading the 42,033-tok floor above, which INCLUDES it.

read-set._: THE PHASE 0 MANDATORY READ -- the pair starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md orders read IN FULL before any work, plus SAFEGUARDS.md which its step 1 orders read in full too. This class exists SEPARATELY from read-mandated because that class here holds the ledgers (CHANGELOG.md, HANDOFFS.md, docs/planning/BACKLOG.md, ~320 KB); totalling those together with the 70 KB procedure pair would produce a number that partitions nothing. total_bytes is NOT typed: derive_from_read_cap makes it READ_CAP_BYTES - adopter_reserve_bytes, computed at run time, and a disagreement with the value written here is reported as a config defect rather than silently honoured. See upstream-read-set-pr-plan.md 3.4(c). warn_bytes 51,000 is one SAFEGUARDS.md-sized edit (15,386 B) short of nothing useful; it sits ~10% under the total so the warning arrives before the refusal does.

files._: max_lines 200 is THIS FRAMEWORK'S OWN PUBLISHED NUMBER, not an invention: starter-kit/BOOTSTRAP.md:199 says 'Claude Code targets roughly 200 lines' and tells adopters to extract to a referenced PROJECT_LEARNINGS.md before that budget is crowded. Dogfooding it here is the whole point of BL-37. max_bytes converts it at this file's measured density — 11,064 B / 119 lines = 92.97 B/line, x200 = 18,594 B, rounded to 18,600 — because a line ceiling alone just produces longer lines. warn_bytes sits 2,600 B below, which is two of the largest single-session increases this file has actually taken since the S24 cut (+1,308 B at d69f7a9, +1,017 B at 316e7ef), so the warning arrives with about two sessions of notice. NO protected_fence IS DECLARED, deliberately: the seed's budget:protected fence does not exist in this file, and declaring it without adding it would report 'over' for a missing fence — a red manufactured by this config rather than a real defect. Adding the fence edits canonical content that ships upstream; raised as a follow-on instead.

files._: NO max_tokens SINCE S177 (2026-09-16, resync stage M2, operator decision). The 25,000 declared at 97c8066 is what the tool derives anyway, by clamping max_bytes / 2.27 to the read cap, so the verdict is unchanged. It was dropped because upstream's TestThisRepoReadSetPartition (tools/test_context_budget.py) then summed the declared max_tokens of every whole-read class against ONE 25,000-token Read, and this class's two ledgers are separate reads. Since BL-62 (5223afb, merged at 5f5a400) the test sums only the read-set pair; the declaration stays dropped, because the clamp derives the same 25,000. Read-mandated: Phase 0 step 6 reconciles this file's frontier and Phase 3A reads the predecessor's receipt in full. max_lines 1,200 is THIS FILE'S OWN DECLARED TRIGGER, stated in its front matter ('Archive again ... when this one approaches ~1,200 lines'), which is tighter than the 2,000-line Read cap and so governs. MAX_BYTES 65,536 IS RETAINED BUT NO LONGER THE OPERATIVE GUARD, and S98 measured why. Across 81 transcripts of this repo (the measuring session excluded, heredoc bodies stripped, classified per PIPELINE so `git show f | grep x` counts once): the live root ledger was read WHOLE into a session's context exactly ONCE and read in PART 593 times -- median span 25 lines, largest ever requested 220, against a 452-line file. No read in the corpus asked for even half of it. So the whole-file ceiling guards a cost paid once in 81 sessions, while the cost paid 593 times -- one RECORD, which is what the sentence above already said Phase 3A reads -- had no guard at all. THE GUARD IS NOW `RECORD_BUDGET_BYTES = 12288` IN bin/check-handoff (CANONICAL-ONLY, not in bin/_manifest.py), scoped to the record being written, with the evidence and the fit assertion beside the constant. IT IS A POLICY NUMBER, NOT A DERIVATION -- and that changed at S106 (2026-08-25). It was 18 KiB, derived as (65,536 - 8,000) / 3 = 19,178 rounded down, a formula that fits the budget TO the ceiling and so sized it as large as would fit; steady state 3 x 18 KiB + 8,000 = 63,296 B, only 2,240 B of slack, which forced a trim nearly every session while never touching the ~25 KB a session actually pays. The formula's only remaining job is the assertion 3 x budget + header reserve <= 65,536: 3 x 12,288 + 8,000 = 44,864 B, 68.5% of the ceiling, 20,672 B of slack -- more than one whole receipt. 12,288 was chosen because a receipt's FENCED fields mean 12,108 B while its TRAILING PROSE (the Phase 3A/3B essays, additive to the six mandatory requirements) is 27-30% of it, so the cut lands on the essays; ratified by the operator over costed alternatives 10,240 and 8,192, evidence in docs/planning/record-budget-reduction-plan.md. The floor of 3 is bin/tests.sh Test 34's, not the methodology's. Records have grown 3.15x: oldest 10 mean 5,478 B, newest 10 mean 17,258 B, largest ever 21,267 B (n=104, live + archives). WHY THE CEILING STAYS AND IS NOT LOWERED TO MATCH: it is what the derivation is computed FROM, and it is still the trim trigger -- `methodology_trim.py --file HANDOFFS.md --check` keys on it. Under the OLD derived reading, lowering it would silently re-derive the record budget downward on the next read of this note; that mechanism is gone now that the budget is policy, but the trim-trigger reason stands on its own. Its source is `methodology_trim.py`'s DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES at :80 (this entry said :69 until S98; S97 flagged the drift and left it, FM #17 -- the CHANGELOG.md entry's copy of the same stale citation is UNTOUCHED and still reads :69). EXPECT THIS ENTRY TO REPORT over WHENEVER A CLOSE-OUT HAS JUST APPENDED A RECEIPT AND NO TRIM HAS RUN YET -- that is the trim trigger doing its job, not a defect; the durable question is whether the RECORD budget is green. NO max_line_bytes, deliberately and unlike the seed's SESSION_NOTES.md entry: the handoff block format is one field per line by design, so field lines run to thousands of bytes legitimately, and a per-line ceiling here would fight the format bin/check-handoff enforces rather than find a defect. **DECOUPLED FROM THE TRIMMER, S116 (2026-08-26), Phase C2 -- AND ONE CLAUSE ABOVE IS NOW FALSE.** *"it is still the trim trigger -- `methodology_trim.py --file HANDOFFS.md --check` keys on it"* no longer holds: option C1 raised `DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES` to 196,608 B and Phase C2 gave root Class A ledgers a 196,608 B archive arm, so `--check` on this file now reports **trigger does not fire** at sizes that fired yesterday. The ceiling is kept at 65,536 anyway, for the OTHER reason already stated above -- it is what the A1 fit assertion in `bin/check-handoff` is computed from -- but that is now its ONLY remaining warrant, and the `:80` citation is stale (the constant is at `:127`). **Consequence for the sentence after this one:** an `over` report here right after a close-out is no longer "the trim trigger doing its job"; it is this fork's own read-cost ceiling speaking, and the trimmer will stay silent until 192 KiB. The durable question is unchanged: is the RECORD budget green?

The verdict is unchanged. THE CEILING IS THE CLASS TOTAL MINUS ITS SIBLING'S, so the two per-file ceilings SUM to read-set.total_bytes exactly: 56,750 - 15,386 = 41,364. That is what makes the class ceiling a PARTITION rather than a second, unrelated number -- per-file ceilings alone do not sum, and bytes moved from SAFEGUARDS.md into this file would leave both rows green with the Phase 0 read unchanged. This file is 54,363 B today, so it is 12,999 B OVER on arrival and every commit that grows it is refused while every commit that shrinks it passes: a ratchet, not a wall. Being over on arrival is the POINT -- the plan exists because the pair is over the one-read cap.

max_tokens 6,777 SINCE S177: int(15,386 / 2.27), declared for the same reason as SESSION_RUNNER.md's 18,222; the verdict is unchanged. THE CEILING IS THIS FILE'S CURRENT SIZE, which is a deliberate no-growth pin rather than a measurement dressed as a budget. Two reasons it is the right half to freeze: it is BYTE-IDENTICAL on upstream/main (blob f0964195), so pinning it here cannot diverge the two trees; and it is the smaller, stabler half, so the remedy the plan actually wants -- shrinking SESSION_RUNNER.md -- is where the whole 12,999 B of headroom debt sits. At exactly 15,386 B the file is AT its ceiling, not over: `new > ceil` is strict, so today's content passes and the next byte does not.

_synced: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and this is an inversion worth stating rather than an omission. The seed ships two synced entries (SESSION_RUNNER.md, SAFEGUARDS.md) that drift-check an adopter's local copy against a canonical checkout elsewhere. THIS REPO IS THAT CANONICAL. It holds no local copies to drift -- starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md and starter-kit/SAFEGUARDS.md ARE the originals -- so the naive adaptation, pointing path and canonical at the same file, would git hash-object the same blob twice and compare it to itself: an assertion of an identity that no change can falsify, which is the exact 'comment shaped like a guard' this repo has already had to delete once (fork Learning #16). THE OTHER HALF OF THE INVERSION IS NOW ACTED ON. The seed says synced files are drift-checked and never size-checked because an adopter may not edit them, so a size finding would be unactionable. Here they ARE editable, so a size finding IS actionable -- and as of S129 those two files carry per-file ceilings in files[] under the read-set class. THAT IS WHY THEY ARE IN files[] AND NOT HERE: check_synced() is drift-only by its own docstring, sets no `bytes` and no `class`, and main() routes synced[] to a list that never enters any aggregate, so a max_bytes written into a synced entry looks configured and refuses nothing. Sizes today: SESSION_RUNNER.md 54,363 B, SAFEGUARDS.md 15,386 B (wc -c, 2026-08-30); the 52,386 B that stood here for SESSION_RUNNER.md was 1,977 B stale.

The note that stood here said ceilings for them were 'NOT taken (FM #17), measured and raised instead'; they were raised, the operator ranked the work, and it is done, so the exclusion is retired rather than left contradicting files[]. It also carried starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md at 52,386 B, which was 1,977 B STALE -- the file is 54,363 B (wc -c, 2026-08-30). Never derive a ceiling from a size written in prose. Its losslessness is proved by docs/planning/BACKLOG-DETAIL.md.verify.sh, not by a ceiling. Adding any of these means declaring a ceiling nobody has defended yet, which is policy, not provisioning. CHANGELOG.md LEFT files[] 2026-09-14 (S161 follow-up, operator decision): it was declared read-mandated because Phase 0 step 6 reconciles it and Phase 3F writes to it, but neither reads it whole -- the reconcile's frontier and gap come from `git log`, a close-out prepends under the topmost month heading, and (the operator's rationale) a session looking for something greps or runs git, so only those results enter its context. Its 65,536 B / 2,000-line / 25,000-token ceilings therefore priced a whole-file read that no session makes; the line half of that argument is BL-52's. Its size stays bounded by starter-kit/methodology_trim.py's own 196,608 B Class A trigger, which asks the question that remains: whether archiving is worth doing. The removed entry, with its S116 decoupling note, is recoverable with `git show bb6eb72:.context-budget.json`.
